title: Multiple Response (same model formula) Optimizer
labelAnalysisTime: Be Patient! Response optimization will take longer if many response variables are selected or categorical variables are used in the model formula, each with a lot of values
labelModelResponseValues: Variables (factors) in selected model listed below in the same order they appear in the model
formulaboxhint: You can also enter SO(var1, var2,...) for second-order effects quadretic PQ() and interactions TWI(), and main effect FO()
instructionLabel: Specify comma-separated values - one value for each model
goal: Goal: (Specify minimize, maximize, target, or range)
target: Target: Specify target values of the responses
lower: Lower: Specify minimum acceptable values of the responses (if left blank, model response min value will be used)
upper: Upper: Specify maximum acceptable values of the responses (if left blank, model response max value will be used)
weight: Weight: Specify Weight values (i.e., penalty for being away from target) of the responses (must be > 0, if left empty, 1 for each model)
importance: Importance: Specify importance for each response to combine multiple responses (must be > 0, if left empty, 1 for each model)
label200: Model Predictor Numeric Variable Constraints for Response Optimizer
label12: Constraint values for the numeric predictor variables must be specified in the same order they appear across all models (hint: run the dialog with default constraints once to see the order of the numeric variables across all models)
factorConstraintUseDatasetLowerChk: Lower Bound Constraints: If checked, minimum (for numeric variables only) value of each variable used in the model will be used for lower bound
factorConstraintLower: Lower Bound Constraints: (Ignored if checked above) Leave empty for no constraints on the lower bound for the model variable values. Otherwise, you must type comma-separated values for every model variable. If a particular model variable has no lower bound, type -Inf, e.g., 0, 0.1, -Inf, 20
factorConstraintUseDatasetUpperChk: Upper Bound Constraints: If checked, maximum (for numeric variables only) value of each variable used in the model will be used for upper bound
factorConstraintUpper: Upper Bound Constraints: (Ignored if checked above) Leave empty for no constraints on the upper bound for the model variable values. Otherwise, you must type comma-separated values for every model variable. If a particular model variable has no upper bound, type Inf, e.g., 0, 0.2, 0.9, Inf
factorInitalValues: Starting Values: Leave empty for system to choose the initial starting values for model variable (for numeric variables only) values (default: all zeros). Otherwise, you must type comma-separated values for every model variable, e.g., 0, 0, 0, 0
showOptimConstraintsChk: Show optimization constraints used for the numeric predictor variables
showEachModelOptimizationChk: Show optimization for each Response model
showModelDetailsChk: Show each model details (click to enable the following options)
showModelMixMaxValuesChk: Show min, max values and categorical levels of the model parameter
showModelVarDetailsChk: show data type of the model parameters
saveModelChk: Save all the models for later use with the Model Evaluation menu
supressPredictWarningsChk: Supress warnings from internal prediction computations
